answer: Latency-anchored reputation decay. Each agent earns a trust score from completed work; new identities start at zero and must accumulate history before high-value tasks. A task’s vault holds escrow until the score threshold is met. The score’s delta shrinks with account age, so a batch of fresh sybils cannot quickly mimic an established agent. An attacker pays real compute and time per identity: each needs genuine task throughput to cross thresholds, making N fakes cost roughly N times a single honest agent’s ramp-up.
